verdict: changes requested before strict preference replacement integration

findings.title: Recovery resend bypasses persisted predecessor policy
findings.scenario: After a strict missing-anchor replacement is durably saved and reopened, an older attempt reappears pending while the current candidate is dropped but valid. inspectReplacement reports pending and assertReplacementPredecessors rejects, yet recover/reconcilePrevious use recoverSaved, validate only the current candidate, and broadcast it. This is realistic before either competing attempt is included and violates the planned no-resend-while-any-prior-live fence.
findings.reproduction: execution/evidence/G07/replacement-cf84551-recover-probe.json uses actual SDK Tx bytes and AEAD with labelled node replies; one send observed despite pending predecessor, ciphertext unchanged.
findings.repair: For persisted strict replacement records, recheck every predecessor immediately before recovery broadcast, bind exact operation/current hash/ciphertext and recheck wallet context. Do not reject read-only reconciliation of an already canonical current transaction. Preserve legacy non-strict behavior. Cover recover and reconcilePrevious after restart, pending/canonical/unknown/changed-reason predecessors and CAS during validation; no sends and original encrypted history retained.

positiveDisposition: Read-only inspection is detached/frozen and does not write/acknowledge/authorize; canonical predecessor is separately identified, not declared current success.
All exact predecessor/current Tx bytes authenticated and re-encoded; full operation/current hash/CAS checked; eight predecessor cap retained.
Strict only-missing-anchor mode persisted after prepare and cannot be downgraded by omitted/false options on the new inspection/authorization/guard methods.
Prepare rereads authenticated prior state instead of trusting caller-mutated decoded fields; same operation/application-nullifier legacy validation retained.
Time-bounded inspection disables follow-up reads after expiry; unknown transport/schema failures never grant authority and raw diagnostics are suppressed.
Existing finality guard and portable encrypted journal tests retained.
requiredLaterIntegration: Production application must retain original expectedRevision and immutable business input, require explicit marker-context and fee review, and consume strict prior guard in the real existing beforeSubmit path.
Bounded paid inclusion/fee history must remain recoverable across reorg; new journal API alone does not establish this history.

Fresh authenticated preference replay, reorg/pool invalidation/reinclusion, cold restore and same-revision contract uniqueness need actual integrated evidence; labelled random proofs do not establish them.
Advanced-head/concurrent-device recovery remains separate and unresolved.
